samples.summary: The new cut suite pins every branch of the image-cut path except the read-only one, leaving the authz gate that makes it safe untested
samples.evidence:
The delta adds four tests that pin the click-selected-image cut path, including that it mutates the document (`writes the image to the clipboard and removes it from the doc`, copy-integrity.test.ts:329-345). None of them constructs a read-only editor.

That matters because of the gate ordering the delta itself documents at copy-integrity.test.ts:311-312: `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:2298) consumes Cmd/Ctrl+X and returns `true`, so `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` returns at text-editor.ts:855 and NEVER reaches its own read-only gate at text-editor.ts:883. The keystroke is therefore ungated at the keyboard layer by design. The only two things standing between a share-link viewer and a document mutation are the duplicated `if (this.readOnly)` in `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1219) and `if (readOnly || !selectedImage)` in `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2243).

Both are correct today — I verified there is no bypass — but a future refactor that drops either one turns viewer Cmd/Ctrl+X on an image into a write, and the suite this delta just wrote would stay green. Attack, if the guard is ever lost: open a read-only share link, click an image, press Cmd/Ctrl+X; `handleCut` reaches `imageDeleteHandler?.()` at text-editor.ts:1230 and the inline is deleted from the shared CRDT. A `readOnly: true` variant of the existing test asserting the inline survives would pin it. (`initialize` takes readOnly as its 4th arg, editor.ts:919.)

samples.summary: `api.selectImageAt` has no read-only guard and is absent from the MUTATING_METHODS allowlist, letting a read-only editor enter image-selection state its own input layer refuses to create
samples.evidence:
`selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3639-3646) sets `selectedImage` and calls `selection.setRange(null)` with no `readOnly` check, and it is not among the methods neutralized for view-only mode at editor.ts:3811-3821. The pointer path that normally produces this state deliberately refuses to in read-only: `handleImageMouseDown` returns at editor.ts:2454 with `if (readOnly) return;`.

This delta is the first caller of `selectImageAt` anywhere in the repo (Grep across packages/ returns only copy-integrity.test.ts), and it wires it directly upstream of the mutating `handleCut` image branch (text-editor.ts:1224-1232) and of `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2242). So the delta newly exposes an API that plants state read-only mode is designed to exclude, immediately in front of two write sinks.

I could not complete an exploit chain: both sinks re-check `readOnly` (text-editor.ts:1219, editor.ts:2243), and `updateSelectedImage` checks it too (editor.ts:3665), so the state is currently inert for a viewer. The residual weakness is defense-in-depth plus one real read-only side effect — `selection.setRange(null)` silently discards a viewer's text selection, which the read-only Copy path in docs-context-menu.tsx:181 depends on. Adding `if (readOnly) return;` at editor.ts:3640 (or listing it alongside the other image methods) keeps the invariant in one place rather than relying on three downstream re-checks.
